title: One Trader Destroyed a 233-Year-Old Bank #shorts
description:
In 1995, a 28-year-old trader in Singapore brought down Barings, the bank of the Queen. Hidden losses, a secret account, and an earthquake.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
first_comment: Who's more to blame: Leeson, or the bank that let one 28-year-old bet it all without checking? 👇

lines.text: In 1995, one trader destroyed a bank that had survived for two hundred and thirty-three years.
His name was Nick Leeson, star trader of Barings, the bank of the Queen.
But his profits were a lie.
Every time he lost, he hid the loss in a secret account. Number 88888.
And he doubled his bets to win it back.
He bet that Japan's market would stay calm.
Then an earthquake struck the city of Kobe.
The market crashed. His losses exploded.
Eight hundred and twenty-seven million pounds. More than the bank's entire capital.
Barings collapsed, and was sold for one pound.
Leeson fled, was caught, and spent years in a Singapore prison.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
